base_member_text: rmse() (L77-81) is not defined in this file and is not a classic built-in; requires an external function on the path.
audit_member_text: The rmse calls at lines 77-81 rely on a function not defined in this file; compatibility depends on an external MATLAB/toolbox or path-provided implementation.

base_member_text: Variable nn is first the record length used in the skewness/asymmetry normalizations (L36, L45, L52) and is then silently redefined as the gauge index range 2:12 (L64) used in plotting and RMSE -- two unrelated meanings in one script.
L34 comment says remove the first 20 seconds but drops 399 samples; with the wavemaker script's dt=0.05 s that is ~20 s, yet the sampling interval of these station files is not stated here.
mskew=mskew; and masy=masy; (L59, L61) are no-op self-assignments; bare string expressions at L14 and L29 serve only as progress echoes.
Header calls the experiment 'Make-Kirby (1992)' (L1) -- presumably Mase-Kirby per the directory name car_mase_kirby.
Gauge 1 (h=47 cm) is excluded from model curves and RMSE (index nn=2:12, L64) while data curves use all 12 (n=1:12, L63) -- rationale not stated.

audit_member_text: Lines 24-25 index gage(:,2) and assign it into successive columns of en without checking that each loaded station file has a second column or the same row count; a short-column file causes an index error and unequal lengths cause an assignment-size mismatch.

Line 34 assumes at least 400 samples. If length(en)<400 the 400:length(en) index descends rather than representing an empty post-spinup interval, and subsequent statistics can select unintended rows or fail; no bound check is present.
Lines 44-52 divide third moments by standard deviations cubed without guarding zero or non-finite variance, so a constant/empty station series yields NaN or Inf and defeats the intended statistic.

Lines 77-81 divide RMSE by max(ske) or max(ae) without a zero/non-finite guard; because max is also a signed reference maximum rather than a magnitude scale, all-nonpositive reference data can produce a negative percentage.

nhn is assigned at line 38 but never consumed, while nn is first a scalar sample count at line 36 and later deliberately overwritten as the 2:12 plotting/RMSE index at line 64; any later insertion expecting the sample count would silently receive an index vector.
